title: What Would Europe Do in a Taiwan Crisis?
author: Simona Grano
text:
Credit: Pixabay
Imagine that, one morning, Chinese coast guard vessels begin stopping commercial ships approaching Taiwan. Beijing offers the official explanation that the operation is necessary to enforce customs regulations and maritime safety and makes clear that it does not consider this a blockade, let alone an act of war. Taipei clearly sees things differently and calls it an attempt to blockade the island. Washington agrees with Taipei.Europe, however, is less certain, with some governments demanding that China stop its actions while others start calling for restraint and dialogue. Officials begin debating whether the operation constitutes an armed attack, what international law permits, and whether sanctions against China would be justified. Meanwhile the effects on global trade start to be felt as insurers raise premiums, shipping companies start to reroute vessels, and financial markets react nervously.[...]
